newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour would shift Budget back to March.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour would shift Budget back to March.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party would move annual Budget presentations back to March if it took power, a party official told Reuters on Tuesday.
"We decided some time ago this would be the case," the official said.
The Conservative government switched the Budget to November, from its traditional slot in March, in 1993.

The Labour official told Reuters that shadow Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown hoped the move would quash government claims that Labour would hold two budgets within a few months of coming to power, implying tax and spending increases.
The Evening Standard newspaper quoted a Labour leadership source as saying the move back would be "sensible and popular."
The Labour Party has pledged to hold a budget within weeks of coming to power. Elections are due by May and Labour leads by up to 20 points in the opinion polls.
Brown has promised to match Conservative spending plans for the first two years of a Labour government and said he would not raise income tax over the life of the next government.
The Evening Standard said Labour leaders think the autumn parliamentary timetable is too crowded to hold the budget. Party conferences and the Queen's speech all happen around the same time.
"It is clear that the November budget has not been popular with the City or in Parliament," the paper quoted its Labour source as saying.

It said Brown had not decided whether to hold a joint taxation and public spending budget in March or return to the old system where a spring Budget would outline broad tax proposals, with spending plans announced separately in an autumn statement.
